questions.text: A principle paragraph in a CLAT item reads: "A person is liable for negligence if he owes a duty of care to the plaintiff, breaches that duty, and causes damage thereby, unless the plaintiff voluntarily assumed the risk." Which of the following correctly identifies the structural elements a candidate must underline while reading this principle?

options.label: A
options.text: Only the three positive conditions: duty of care, breach, and causation of damage.

options.label: B
options.text: The three positive conditions plus the qualifying phrase "unless the plaintiff voluntarily assumed the risk" as an exception.

options.label: C
options.text: The three positive conditions, but the "unless" clause is merely explanatory and not an operative exception.

options.label: D
options.text: The principle contains no exceptions because "unless" introduces a defence, not an element of the principle.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The three positive conditions plus the qualifying phrase "unless the plaintiff voluntarily assumed the risk" as an exception..

questions.text: According to the lesson, what is the typical function of the final paragraph in a contemporary RC passage?

options.label: A
options.text: To introduce the central issue and define key terms

options.label: B
options.text: To present the author's personal biography and credentials

options.label: C
options.text: To offer a synthesis, recommendation, or forward-looking observation

options.label: D

questions.solution: Correct answer: To offer a synthesis, recommendation, or forward-looking observation.

questions.text: Under which Act was the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India established?

questions.text: According to the lesson, what is the critical distinction between the analytical process required for Legal Reasoning questions and that for General Knowledge questions in CLAT?

options.label: A
options.text: Legal Reasoning requires memorizing statutory provisions, while General Knowledge requires logical deduction.

options.label: B
options.text: Legal Reasoning demands a structured sequential process of isolating the rule, then the facts, then matching them, whereas General Knowledge relies on factual recall.

options.label: C
options.text: General Knowledge questions test the ability to apply principles to facts, while Legal Reasoning questions test awareness of current legal affairs.

options.label: D
options.text: Both sections follow the same analytical method, but Legal Reasoning uses longer passages.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Legal Reasoning demands a structured sequential process of isolating the rule, then the facts, then matching them, whereas General Knowledge relies on factual recall..

questions.text: The Government announces a policy to regularize all ad-hoc employees with 10 years of service. Relying on this, an employee declines a private job offer. Before regularization, the Government withdraws the policy citing fiscal constraints, without hearing the employee. The employee challenges the withdrawal. Which principle governs the outcome?

options.label: A
options.text: The employee has a substantive right to regularization because the policy created a legitimate expectation enforceable as a contract.

options.label: B
options.text: The withdrawal is valid because legitimate expectation is merely a moral claim with no legal enforceability against the State.

options.label: C
options.text: The withdrawal is invalid because legitimate expectation requires a hearing before frustration, unless overriding public interest is shown, which mere fiscal constraints may not satisfy.

options.label: D
options.text: The employee can claim damages for breach of promise under promissory estoppel, but cannot compel regularization.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The withdrawal is invalid because legitimate expectation requires a hearing before frustration, unless overriding public interest is shown, which mere fiscal constraints may not satisfy..

questions.text: A chemical plant operates under a licence that permits emissions of a pollutant up to a specified limit. Due to a sudden equipment failure, the plant releases the pollutant at a level exceeding the licensed limit, damaging nearby crops. Under the Indian absolute liability principle laid down in M. C. Mehta v. Union of India, is the enterprise liable?

options.label: A
options.text: No, because the plant was operating under statutory authority, which is a complete defence.

options.label: B
options.text: No, because the escape occurred despite compliance with the licence conditions.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, because absolute liability imposes responsibility irrespective of compliance with statutory limits and the licence does not authorise the escape.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, but only if the claimant proves negligence in the maintenance of the equipment.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Yes, because absolute liability imposes responsibility irrespective of compliance with statutory limits and the licence does not authorise the escape..

A State Legislature enacts a law imposing a tax on "services rendered by way of legal consultation". The State argues it falls under Entry 62 (taxes on professions) of the State List. The Union argues it encroaches on Entry 97 (residuary power) or constitutes a tax on services (GST domain). The Court finds the true nature of the levy is a tax on the profession of advocates. Which maxim resolves this competence dispute?

options.label: A
options.text: Colourable legislation — the State has misused its power by labelling a service tax as a profession tax.

options.label: B
options.text: Pith and substance — the true character of the legislation determines its legislative competence.

options.label: C
options.text: Ultra vires — the State lacks any power to tax legal services under the Seventh Schedule.

options.label: D
options.text: Basic structure — federalism is violated if States tax professional services exclusively regulated by the Bar Council.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Pith and substance — the true character of the legislation determines its legislative competence..

questions.text: According to the passage, which of the following best describes an implicit assumption in an argument?

options.label: A
options.text: A stated reason supporting the claim.

options.label: B
options.text: An unstated belief necessary for the argument to hold.

options.label: C
options.text: A counterargument presented for refutation.

options.label: D
options.text: A statistical evidence cited by the author.

questions.solution: Correct answer: An unstated belief necessary for the argument to hold..

questions.text: An employee of a courier company, while delivering a package, detours 15 kilometres to visit a friend and causes an accident. The employer argues the employee was on a "frolic of his own". Which factor is decisive for determining whether the employer remains vicariously liable?

options.label: A
options.text: Whether the employer exercised direct control over the manner of driving at the time of the accident

options.label: B
options.text: Whether the act of driving was expressly authorised by the employer

options.label: C
options.text: The degree of deviation from the assigned delivery route and duties

options.label: D
options.text: The employee's personal motive for making the detour

questions.solution: Correct answer: The degree of deviation from the assigned delivery route and duties.

questions.text: How many integers from 1 to 500 inclusive are divisible by at least one of 3, 5, or 7?

options.label: A
options.text: Damage without legal injury — not actionable

options.label: B
options.text: Legal injury without damage — actionable

options.label: C
options.text: Guilty act

options.label: D

questions.solution: Correct answer: Damage without legal injury — not actionable.
